title: Finite congruence monodromy of a residually trivial lisse lattice
statement:
Let $\ell$ be a prime, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ a finite extension with its norm topology, $A=\mathcal O_E$ its valuation ring and $\varpi$ a uniformizer [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Put $A_n=A/\varpi^nA$ for $n\geq1$. Let $X$ be a nonempty connected scheme with a chosen geometric point $\bar x$ [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-connected-scheme, def-weil-geometric-point]. On $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], use the pulled condensed continuous-map rings $A_X$ and $(A_n)_X$, the latter with $A_n$ discrete [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring, sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], and internal modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. Let $N$ be a lisse finite-rank $A_X$-module, where lisse means pro-etale locally a finite direct sum of copies of $A_X$, including rank zero [def-sfb-lisse-coefficient-module]. Let $F_n=N/\varpi^nN$ denote the scalar cokernel, with its actual reduction maps. Write $d\geq0$ for the rank of the finite free fibre of $F_1$ at $\bar x$.

For every $n\geq1$, $F_n$ is the pro-etale inverse image of an etale finite locally constant sheaf of free $A_n$-modules of rank $d$ [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism, def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. These etale models respect the actual transitions $F_{n+1}/\varpi^nF_{n+1}\cong F_n$. This assertion is about the stated pulled condensed coefficients and is preserved by passage to the equivalent category of sheaf modules with the same underlying abelian sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category].

Suppose in addition that $F_1\cong(A_1)_X^d$, where $(A_1)_X$ is the constant finite coefficient sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. For each $n$, let $\rho_n$ be the continuous $A_n$-linear action on the fibre of the etale model induced by the profinite etale fundamental group $\pi_1(X,\bar x)$ [def-galois-fibre-functor, def-galois-categories]. In any basis its image $Q_n$ is a subgroup of
$$K_n=\ker\bigl(\operatorname{GL}_d(A_n)\longrightarrow\operatorname{GL}_d(A_1)\bigr),$$
where $\operatorname{GL}_d(B)$ means the group of invertible $d$-by-$d$ matrices over $B$. Both $K_n$ and $Q_n$ have order a power of $\ell$. There is a connected finite etale surjection $P_n\to X$ equipped with a $Q_n$-action simply transitive on every geometric fibre, that is, a $Q_n$-torsor [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-etale-morphism, def-weil-surjective-morphism, def-sbc-normal-dominant-galois], on which $F_n$ is the constant free rank-$d$ $(A_n)_{P_n}$-module. In particular its group order is prime to every prime $p\ne\ell$. The assertions include $n=1$ and $d=0$, when $Q_n$ is trivial. No common trivializing cover for all $n$ is asserted.

proof.text: For each $n$, multiplication by $\varpi^n$ identifies $A$ homeomorphically with $\varpi^n A$: the inverse divides by the fixed nonzero scalar $\varpi^n$. The quotient $A_n$ is finite and discrete, and its reduction map is continuous, since $\varpi^n A$ is an open additive subgroup (a valuation ball). Apply [lem-pe-profinite-sections-finite-quotient] to $A\xrightarrow{\varpi^n}A\to A_n$. It gives the condensed cokernel $\underline A/\varpi^n\underline A\cong\underline{A_n}$, with the actual reduction projection. The left-adjoint description of $p_X^*$ and [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits] carry this cokernel to $X$. Strong monoidality carries the scalar multiplication to multiplication by the same scalar. Thus $A_X/\varpi^n A_X\cong(A_n)_X$, normalized on the quotient projection. The coefficient definition supplies finiteness and the valuation topology.

proof.text: Choose a lisse trivializing cover, so $N|_{U_i}\cong A_{U_i}^{r_i}$. Restriction preserves cokernels by [lem-trf-geometric-inverse-image-exact], and coefficients restrict to those on $U_i$ by [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients]. Step 1 and finite direct sums give $F_n|_{U_i}\cong(A_n)_{U_i}^{r_i}$, simultaneously for the actual scalar quotients of this $N$. Use the finite-discrete coefficient equivalence [lem-sf-module-object-ordinary-coefficient-equivalence] to regard these as ordinary constant-ring module sheaves, with the same underlying abelian sheaves and free local models. This is valid for arbitrary schemes and all finite $A_n$, without a Noetherian hypothesis.

source.place: Definitions 6.8.1, 6.8.3; Lemma 6.8.2(1), Proposition 6.8.4(1), pp.58-59; finite-level argument supplied explicitly.

proof.text: Apply [det-pe-finite-local-systems-type] to $F_1$: it is locally constant with finitely presented free models over the finite field $A_1$. Its module-type loci are disjoint clopen subschemes. Since $X$ is nonempty and connected, just one type locus is nonempty. The stalk at $\bar x$ has type $A_1^d$, so every nonempty local model has $A_1^{r_i}\cong A_1^d$. Comparing finite cardinalities $|A_1|^{r_i}=|A_1|^d$, with $|A_1|>1$, gives $r_i=d$. Discard empty covering objects. The same cover therefore gives the free rank-$d$ model for every $F_n$.

For each $n$, apply [det-pe-uniform-finite-type-model-etale-cover] with $\Lambda=A_n$ and $M=A_n^d$, and [det-pe-finite-local-systems-twist]. We obtain an etale finite locally constant model $G_n$ of $F_n$, and an etale trivializing cover with the very same free model $A_n^d$. Thus the model is free of rank $d$, not merely finite as a set. The exact module comparison equivalence [sk-thm-pe-classical-sheaves] is fully faithful. The actual quotient identity $(N/\varpi^{n+1}N)/\varpi^n(N/\varpi^{n+1}N)=N/\varpi^nN$ follows because $\varpi^{n+1}N\subseteq\varpi^nN$: both sides are the quotient by the same relations. Exactness and full faithfulness uniquely descend this identity and its reduction map to $G_{n+1}/\varpi^nG_{n+1}\cong G_n$. All iterated transitions agree because they agree after the faithful inverse image. The equivalence of step 2 preserves these cokernels on the same underlying abelian sheaves.

Apply the finite-coefficient clause (1) of [cor-galois-lisse-representations] to $G_n$. Its fibre is a free $A_n$-module of rank $d$, and the resulting action $\rho_n$ is continuous and $A_n$-linear. Compose the actual transitions of step 4 from level $n$ to level $1$. Their scalar-quotient identities give $A_1\otimes_{A_n}G_n\cong G_1$, with the given reduction map. The scalar-compatibility clause therefore identifies the reduced action $A_1\otimes_{A_n}\rho_n$ with the action on the fibre of $G_1$. Under the residual-triviality hypothesis, $G_1$ is constant: its comparison pullback is constant and comparison is fully faithful. The constant sheaf corresponds to the trivial representation, so every matrix of $\rho_n$ reduces to $I_d$. This proves $Q_n\subseteq K_n$ in every basis; changing basis conjugates the matrices and still reduces the identity to the identity.

The local-field input [lem-sf-bc-adic-ring-domain] gives $\ell\in\varpi A$, since $A/\varpi A$ has characteristic $\ell$, and $A_n$ is finite. Fix $n$ and work in $M_d(A_n)$. If $h=I_d+B$ and all entries of $B$ lie in $\varpi^iA_n$, $i\geq1$, then the binomial expansion (valid since $I_d$ commutes with $B$) is $h^\ell=I_d+\ell B+\sum_{j=2}^{\ell}\binom{\ell}{j}B^j$. The first nonconstant term has entries in $\varpi^{i+1}A_n$; all other terms do too, since $ij\geq i+1$ for $j\geq2$. Starting at $i=1$, induction on $a$ gives $g^{\ell^a}-I_d\in\varpi^{a+1}M_d(A_n)$ for every $g\in K_n$. At $a=n-1$ the right side is zero. This is one binomial calculation, including $\ell=2$ and ramified extensions; it does not assume an unramified coefficient ring.

proof.text: The set of matrices over finite $A_n$ is finite, hence so are $K_n$ and its subgroup $Q_n$. Step 6 shows that every element of either group has $\ell^{n-1}$-th power equal to the identity; for $Q_n$ the subgroup inclusion preserves products and the identity. Apply [lem-sfb-finite-group-prime-power-exponent] separately to these two finite groups. It yields $|K_n|=\ell^a$ and $|Q_n|=\ell^b$ for some $a,b\geq0$.

source.place: IsPGroup.iff_card, lines 102-106, applied after the explicit binomial calculation.

proof.text: Put $H_n=\ker(\rho_n)$. This is open and normal, since the target is a finite discrete group and $\rho_n$ is continuous. Apply the pointed classification [cor-galois-open-subgroups] to obtain a pointed connected finite etale cover $(P_n,p_n)$ with stabilizer $H_n$ and degree $[\pi_1:H_n]=|Q_n|>0$. In particular it is surjective: at every point the finite locally free fibre has this positive rank, so its finite algebra over the residue field is nonzero and has a prime ideal. By [thm-galois-fundamental], its fibre is the transitive coset action $\pi_1/H_n\cong Q_n$. Explicitly $gH_n\mapsto\rho_n(g)$ is well defined and bijective; transitivity follows from connectedness via [lem-galois-transitive] and [lem-galois-finite-etale-connected-object]. On $Q_n$ with left $\pi_1$-action $q\mapsto\rho_n(g)q$, the maps $q\mapsto q a^{-1}$ define a commuting left $Q_n$-action. Full faithfulness lifts these maps to $X$-automorphisms of $P_n$, and lifts their group law.

The map $Q_n\times P_n\to P_n\times_XP_n$, $(a,z)\mapsto(z,a\cdot z)$, is an isomorphism: on the chosen fibre it is the bijection $(a,q)\mapsto(q,q a^{-1})$, whose inverse sends $(q,r)$ to $(r^{-1}q,q)$. Full faithfulness and finite-limit compatibility of [thm-galois-fundamental] reflect this bijection as an isomorphism of finite etale covers (the finite disjoint union on the left corresponds to the product with the finite constant set). Base changing the isomorphism shows simple transitivity on every geometric fibre, all of which are nonempty by step 8. Hence this is a $Q_n$-torsor. The same theorem identifies the map on fundamental groups from $P_n$ with the stabilizer $H_n$. Therefore its action on the pulled-back fibre of $G_n$ is trivial. The finite-coefficient equivalence of [cor-galois-lisse-representations], applied on the connected scheme $P_n$, identifies this pullback with the constant $A_n^d$-module sheaf. Comparison and the finite-discrete equivalence in step 2 give precisely the asserted trivialization of $F_n$.

For a prime $p\ne\ell$, the integer $\ell^b$ is prime to $p$, proving the final assertion. If $n=1$, then $K_1$ is the kernel of an identity homomorphism and is trivial. If $d=0$, the group of automorphisms of the zero module is trivial at every level. In either case $Q_n=1$, and the pointed cover of index one is $X$ itself, trivializing the zero module or the assumed constant residue module as appropriate. Every construction was made for a fixed $n$; no choice of a single cover for all levels occurred.
